markdown:
# Product foundation

## Product
Chaser, a working name and not fixed, sends polite payment reminders and collects the payment for freelance designers, so they stop chasing late invoices by hand.

## Problem
Freelance designers hate asking for money. Today they keep a spreadsheet and write awkward emails weeks after the due date, or let it slide. They lose a few hours a month on it.

## Persona
A freelance brand or web designer working alone, with 3 to 10 active clients. They invoice from a tool like Wave or from a PDF. They want the money without asking for it. Hating the ask stops them.

## Core scenario
On a Monday morning at their desk, on a laptop, a designer sees an invoice two weeks overdue. They want to hand it to Chaser in under a minute and not think about it again until the money lands. It happens a few times a month.

## Also affected
The designer's clients, who get the reminders. They should feel nudged, not accused.

## Not for
- Agencies with a finance person.
- Freelancers outside design (developers, writers, consultants). We turn them away at sign-up.

## Feel
Calm, friendly, a bit dry.
Never pushy, corporate or cute.

## Goals
1. 50 paying users by the end of March 2027. A paying user is any user on a paid plan, at any price.
2. $5,000 monthly revenue by the end of December 2027.

Earns by: See Open.

## Anti-goals
1. We will not build invoicing itself.
2. No mobile app.

## Assumptions
Designers will let a tool email their clients in their name.

## Open
- Goals: Earns by is empty. Nothing says how Chaser makes money, or what the paid plan is or costs.
- Goals: Goal 2 does not say if "revenue" is Chaser's own income or the payments it collects for designers.
- Anti-goals: Neither anti-goal says why.
- Anti-goals: Collecting payment from the start may pull against "We will not build invoicing itself". Nothing says where the line falls.
- Core scenario: How an invoice reaches Chaser (Wave, PDF, other) is not said.
- Not for: How sign-up tells a designer from another freelancer is not said.
- Assumptions: Nothing says how or when we will test the one assumption.

questions.question: What evidence do you have that designers lose real money or time to late invoices, and that they would pay to stop it?
questions.why: The Problem is an unsupported claim ("a few hours a month"), and if the pain is small, 50 paying users and $5,000 a month are out of reach.
options: I lost money this way myself

questions.question: If designers refuse to let a tool email their clients in their name, what is the fallback?
questions.why: This one assumption carries the whole product, and the document names no test for it and no alternative if it fails.

questions.question: What do designers use today to chase payment, and why would they switch to Chaser?
questions.why: Wave and similar invoicing tools already send automatic reminders, so the document must say what Chaser does that they and a spreadsheet do not.
options: Chasing is not what they buy

questions.question: When does a designer hand an invoice to Chaser: only once it is overdue, or when they send it, before any due date?
questions.why: The scenario shows an invoice two weeks late, but the Problem and the product (reminders and collecting payment) could begin at sending, and each pictures a different moment and a different first reminder.

questions.question: Which designers count as design: only brand and web designers, or also UI, product, graphic and illustrators?
questions.why: Sign-up turns away non-designers, so the line decides who is refused, and the Persona names only brand and web designers.

questions.question: Do reminders reach the client in the designer's voice or in Chaser's, and does the client pay on a page branded as the designer's or Chaser's?
questions.why: The clients are the people most affected, and 'a bit dry' reads very differently from the designer than from an unknown tool.

questions.question: Where is the line between "no invoicing" and collecting payment: may Chaser make a pay page, a receipt, or a payment-plan split for an invoice made elsewhere?
questions.why: Collecting payment was decided, so without a line any payment-side feature (pay page, receipts, part payments) could be argued to be invoicing or not.

questions.question: Will Chaser ever go beyond polite nudges to firm notices, late fees or a collections handoff?
questions.why: This is the most tempting growth path for a late-payment product and it would break the "nudged, not accused" feel, so it needs a stated reason either way.

questions.question: Will Chaser ever advance the designer the money before the client pays (factoring or a loan)?
questions.why: A product that already holds the payment flow will be tempted to sell advances, which changes the risk, the licensing and what revenue means in Goal 2.

questions.question: How does Chaser earn: what do designers pay, and when?
questions.why: "Earns by" is empty, and "paying user on a paid plan" in goal 1 only makes sense once the plan and price are fixed; $5,000 a month from 50 users also needs about $100 each.

questions.question: In goal 2, does "revenue" mean Chaser's own income or the payments it collects for designers?
questions.why: The two can differ by ten times or more, and the goal is not checkable on a date until the number counts one of them.

questions.question: Where does collecting payment stop and invoicing begin?
questions.why: The founder chose to collect payment from the start, which may break "We will not build invoicing itself", so the line has to be drawn in the document.
